purpose: Research-only evidence packet for five consecutive Dublin City NIAH candidates selected from the latest workflow-generated official missing-registration queue.

official_dataset_reference.title: NIAH Data Download

candidate_records.description_summary: Terraced two-bay four-storey Georgian house over raised basement, built c.1745, with Flemish-bond red brickwork, gauged brick voussoirs, replacement windows, and a round-headed entrance with a painted stone doorcase, Doric pilasters and fanlight.
candidate_records.appraisal_summary: NIAH describes it as a fine Georgian red-brick townhouse; its restrained façade is enlivened by the brickwork and elegant doorcase.
candidate_records.queue_membership: Exact registration 50010232 present in workflow #1991 Dublin City missing-registration queue.

candidate_records.description_summary: Terraced two-bay four-storey house over raised basement, built c.1750 and described by NIAH as now used as retail premises, with Flemish-bond red brickwork, gauged brick voussoirs, granite plinth and sills, and a blocked former entrance with sidelights.
candidate_records.appraisal_summary: NIAH identifies number 79 as retaining much of its early form and character as a Georgian red-brick townhouse; the roof may indicate an earlier Dutch Billy form.
candidate_records.queue_membership: Exact registration 50010233 present in workflow #1991 Dublin City missing-registration queue.
candidate_records.source_field_caution: National CSV IN_USE_AS_TYPE is blank, although the individual NIAH page description says it is now in use as retail premises. Preserve both source values; do not fill the blank CSV field.

candidate_records.description_summary: Terraced two-bay three-storey house, built c.1750, now retail premises, with Flemish-bond red brickwork, parapet-concealed slate roof, a round-headed entrance within a block-and-start stone surround, and a late nineteenth-century shopfront with fluted foliate consoles.
candidate_records.appraisal_summary: NIAH describes a fine late eighteenth-century red-brick townhouse; the surviving block-and-start doorcase and enriched shopfront contribute to its significance.
candidate_records.queue_membership: Exact registration 50010234 present in workflow #1991 Dublin City missing-registration queue.
candidate_records.source_field_caution: National CSV NAME is blank although the individual page title includes a business/trading name. Keep the CSV NAME blank; page title is a separate source label.

candidate_records.name: School of Culinary Arts and Food Technology
candidate_records.address: 66–74 Cathal Brugha Street / Marlborough Street, Dublin 1, Ireland
candidate_records.description_summary: Corner-sited attached four-storey-over-basement Art Deco college, built 1938–39 by Robinson and Keefe, with red brick and granite elevations, a sculptural group of The Three Graces by Gabriel Hayes, and notable original interior finishes.
candidate_records.appraisal_summary: NIAH regards it as one of Dublin's best Art Deco examples, retaining substantial original fabric and interiors; it notes the Three Graces sculpture and its sculptor Gabriel Hayes.
candidate_records.queue_membership: Exact registration 50010236 present in workflow #1991 Dublin City missing-registration queue.

candidate_records.name: Church of Saint George and Saint Thomas
candidate_records.address: Findlater Place / Cathal Brugha Street, Dublin 1, Ireland
candidate_records.description_summary: Freestanding Church of Ireland church built 1930–32, with a gable-fronted nave, granite west portico and columns, two towers, apsidal chancel, red-brick and granite detailing, leaded and coloured glass, and original wrought-iron railings.
candidate_records.appraisal_summary: NIAH identifies the church as a local landmark designed by Frederick Hicks in a Byzantine/Lombardic-Romanesque style, with stained glass by Catherine O'Brien and an apse mosaic by Oppenheimer.
candidate_records.queue_membership: Exact registration 50010237 present in workflow #1991 Dublin City missing-registration queue.
